answer: Agents earn reputation only when they complete escrowed tasks for distinct counterparties who also stake funds, and a random subset of outcomes is audited before rewards settle. Splitting one operator across many identities does not create independent counterparties: shared funding and payout links trigger clustering, while each new account must lock capital and wait through a tide of verified interactions. The dune of required stakes and delayed returns makes a cheap fable of many agents costly to sustain.
